questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part in the braking unit that lets air move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag warns the driver of low air pressure. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost
When a dashboard control is activated
When tires have minimal tread depth

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost
questions.explanation: Spring brakes engage automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. You should safely exit the road as soon as you see the low pressure warning and bring your vehicle to a stop while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Should you refuel a bus while passengers are on board?

options.text: Yes, it is encouraged during long trips
Yes, as long as passengers stay inside
Yes, to show passengers there is enough fuel

questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless it is absolutely necessary. Never refuel inside an enclosed building with passengers on board.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: Scan the road constantly to spot hazards early. Plan ahead for how you will handle hazards if they become dangerous.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating found?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a specific pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: How fast does the body remove alcohol?

options.text: At a rate that changes based on the amount of alcohol in the body
At a consistent rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body
More quickly if the person drinks coffee
More quickly if the person stays awake

questions.correctAnswerText: At a consistent rate, no matter how much alcohol is in the body
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate that cannot be sped up by coffee, cold showers, or other tricks. The only way to sober up is to let your body process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: What happens if a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working?

options.text: The truck will have no brakes
The truck should only be driven at slow speeds
The truck will still have brakes
The truck will have no brakes on its left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the vehicle still has regular braking function. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Scan the road constantly to spot hazards early. Plan ahead for how you will handle hazards if they become dangerous.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle easier to see at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for front tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake system, when you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves the:
questions.explanation: Air pressure pushes rods out of the brake chambers. This moves the slack adjusters and twists the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold only enough air for one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor breaks.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for you to use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What must you do before driving a bus?

options.text: Read the most recent inspection report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the most recent inspection report.
questions.explanation: Always read the inspection report from the previous driver before driving a bus. Only drive the bus if any listed problems have been fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop driving and sleep when you feel sleepy. Trying to stay awake causes crashes. Energy pills are not safe because they only hide tiredness—you become even more tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: Between three-quarters of a second and one second.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters of a second and one second.
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one second.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must leak no more than 3 psi in one minute. Faster leakage means something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: How should you store baggage and freight on a bus?

options.text: In a way that lets riders exit through any door or window in an emergency.
In a way that blocks an exit if other exits are available.
In a way that partially covers a door since items can be moved.
In a way that makes cargo easy to unload in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that lets riders exit through any door or window in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Store baggage and freight so drivers can move freely, riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and items won't fall or shift and hurt riders.

questions.question: In a convex mirror, objects look ____ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors make objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.
